title: French Louisiana
capsule: French Louisiana denotes the short-lived return of Louisiana to French sovereignty under the Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1800), by which Spain retroceded the colony to Napoleon Bonaparte's France. Napoleon intended Louisiana as the provisioning base for Saint-Domingue, but the Haitian Revolution's destruction of the French army under Leclerc, combined with the renewal of war with Britain in 1803, forced him to sell the entire territory to the United States in the Louisiana Purchase (30 April 1803) for approximately 80 million francs. French administrative authority was formally transferred to Spain in November 1803 and then to the United States on 20 December 1803, meaning France never exercised effective administrative control during this period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The boundaries of French Louisiana (1800–1803) are well established from the 1762 Treaty of Fontainebleau and Spanish colonial records, though the western border with New Spain remained disputed.
